channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: PT apostava em votos de Ciro Nogueira e de 7 senadores do PL para aprovar Messias ao STF
item.description: The PT had projected 45 secure votes for Jorge Messias’s STF nomination, including Ciro Nogueira and seven PL senators, but the nomination was rejected with 42 against and only 34 in favor — the first presidential STF defeat since 1894. The PT’s political strategy was blamed for overestimating support, while government allies accused Flávio Dino and alleged a 'coup' by Moraes and Alcolumbre.

item.title: Lula e Messias têm novo papo; permanência na AGU ganha força por enquanto
item.description: President Lula and Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias held a new meeting on Monday (4) to discuss next steps following the Senate's rejection of Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court. Despite the congressional setback, there is growing support for the idea that Messias will remain in his current position as AGU, at least for now, with no immediate moves toward a new nomination or departure.

item.title: Quem lidera a disputa para a Presidência na eleição de 2026? Veja o agregador de pesquisas da BBC News Brasil
item.description: According to the BBC News Brasil Polling Aggregator, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leads the 2026 presidential race with 40% of voter intention in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 37% and Renan Santos at 4%. In the runoff scenario, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are in a technical tie, with 45% and 46% respectively, indicating a highly competitive election.

item.title: Supremo vê erro do Executivo na derrota de Messias
item.description: Supreme Court ministers attribute Jorge Messias's Senate rejection to a political misreading by the Lula government, which underestimated congressional resistance due to its minority bloc. The third Lula term's political articulation is compared to Dilma Rousseff's, with one minister calling it 'Dilma 2 and a half', though without forecasting impeachment. The shift to mandatory parliamentary amendments since 2014 stripped the Executive of its key bargaining tool with Congress, hindering nominee approvals.

item.title: O pedido ao STF do general que tramou assassinar Lula, Alckmin e Moraes
item.description: Retired General Mario Fernandes, sentenced to 26 years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate President Lula, Vice President Alckmin, and Justice Alexandre de Moraes, asked the STF to allow him to pay a R$ 64,800 fine in 60 installments. Despite receiving a net monthly income of R$ 23,000 as a reserve military officer, he claimed the request was necessary to preserve funds for his family’s basic maintenance. Fernandes admitted to drafting the document but described it as a 'digitized thought'.

item.title: Comissão da PEC 6 X 1 inicia trabalhos com tramitação acelerada
item.description: The special committee on the 6x1 work schedule PEC began accelerated proceedings under rapporteur Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA), aiming to reduce the weekly workweek to 36 hours over 4 days and 3 days of rest, abolishing the 6x1 shift. The rapporteur has up to three weeks to draft the proposal, with a transition period capped at five years, as the Lula government pushes for immediate effect upon promulgation, while business groups demand more time to avoid mass layoffs.

item.title: Pix, minerais críticos e tarifas: o que o governo Lula quer discutir com Trump na economia
item.description: President Lula aims to discuss with Trump the review of U.S. investigations into Brazil’s Pix payment system, the removal of remaining tariffs affecting Brazilian exports, and increased investment in critical minerals. These topics, prepared by four ministries, will depend on the White House’s receptiveness ahead of the May 7 meeting.

item.title: Ação no TCU tenta driblar freio a supersalários e cria ‘teto duplex’ para servidores
item.description: An action at the TCU seeks to create a 'duplex ceiling' to circumvent the constitutional monthly salary cap of R$ 46,3 thousand for public servants, targeting trust positions in the Federal Legislature and the TCU itself through bonuses and extra-allowances. The rapporteur, Minister Walton Alencar, received R$ 592 thousand in off-cap payments in 2025, while TCU ministers collectively earned at least R$ 4.3 million in such benefits that year. Despite presidential vetoes and STF rulings against supersalaries, the practice continues via indemnities, medical reimbursements, and performance bonuses.

item.title: Congresso cria precedentes ao rejeitar indicação ao STF e manobrar regimento para não abrir CPI, avaliam técnicos
item.description: The Brazilian Congress set two unprecedented precedents by rejecting the installation of the Banco Master CPMI despite sufficient signatures and by partially overturning an integral presidential veto on the dosimetry bill. These maneuvers, led by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, bypassed long-standing rules and created new interpretations that may be repeated in future legislatures, according to legislative technicians.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0 tenta alcançar classe média: endividados terão alívio até a eleição? Analistas respondem
item.description: President Lula has launched the Desenrola 2.0 measure, expanding the debt relief program to include students, entrepreneurs, and rural farmers earning up to five minimum wages (R$ 8,105), reaching part of the middle class. The initiative aims to ease household debt burdens through 30% to 90% discounts on overdue debts (up to two years old) and allows use of up to 20% or R$ 1,000 from FGTS accounts, as part of a strategy to boost his popularity ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: BR Feminino: São Paulo vence Flamengo para assumir vice-liderança
item.description: São Paulo Women's team defeated Flamengo 2-1 to take second place in the 2026 Brazilian Women's Championship. Goals from Gabi Zanotti and Aline Milene secured the win, with Marta scoring Flamengo's consolation goal. The victory leaves São Paulo just one point behind league leaders Corinthians.

item.title: PF ainda examina contas de Lulinha três meses após autorização do STF
item.description: Three months after the STF authorized the breaking of banking secrecy, the Federal Police continues to analyze the bank accounts of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) in search of evidence of monthly R$300,000 payments allegedly made by lobbyist Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes (Careca do INSS). The investigation is part of the probe into INSS fraud, and while Lulinha’s defense denies involvement and awaits results calmly, investigators admit limitations in detecting cash transfers or those routed through third parties.

item.title: Bolsonaristas veem possível desgaste para Eduardo com reunião entre Lula e Trump
item.description: The upcoming meeting between Lula and Trump in the U.S. has sparked divisions within Bolsonaro's camp: some believe it could weaken Eduardo Bolsonaro due to his close ties with Trump's circle, while others see it as an opportunity for Flávio Bolsonaro to strengthen his oppositional rhetoric by highlighting perceived inconsistencies in the government's foreign policy. Although Flávio's U.S. visit was pre-planned, it is expected to be shaped by the Lula-Trump meeting, with Eduardo's allies denying any setback, while critics argue he already lost influence after the tariff controversy.

item.title: Mesmo proibidos pelo TSE, impulsionamentos de conteúdos online com ataques a adversários se tornam prática frequente do PT e do PL
item.description: Despite being prohibited by the TSE, boosting online content with attacks on adversaries has become a frequent practice for the PT and PL, using Instagram and Facebook ads to accuse Lula and Bolsonaro of crimes and spread misinformation. The PL boosted 18 publications between January and April, five of them accusing Lula of corruption and money laundering, despite those convictions being annulled by the STF. The PT, meanwhile, boosted 17 contents, seven of them attacking Flávio or Jair Bolsonaro, particularly regarding Pix and alleged ties to Trump.

item.title: Da Dona Maria ao Zé da Feira, 'fakes sintéticos' inundam as redes e driblam TSE com narrativas pró e contra governo
item.description: During the 2026 pre-election campaigns, AI-generated avatars known as 'synthfakes' have been used to spread pro- and anti-government Lula narratives on social media, exploiting loopholes in electoral legislation. These synthetic contents, more sophisticated than traditional deepfakes, hinder the TSE's efforts to combat disinformation.

item.title: Com PSD e PL liderando crescimento, um terço dos deputados estaduais do país trocou de partido durante a janela
item.description: Over one-third of Brazil's 1,059 state deputies changed parties during the 2025 partisan window, mainly benefiting the PL and PSD, which gained 34 additional seats. The PSDB saw its presence nearly halved, while small parties failed to expand. Analysts link the shift to post-2024 municipal election power dynamics and governors' influence on local politics.

item.title: Furto, roubo, estelionato e receptação: Lula sanciona lei que prevê aumento de penas no Brasil
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.397/2026, increasing penalties for theft, robbery, fraud, receiving stolen goods, and cybercrimes such as online scams and bank fraud. He vetoed a provision that would have raised the minimum sentence for robbery causing serious bodily injury above that for qualified homicide, citing disproportionality. The law also imposes stricter penalties for theft of cell phones, wires, cables, and essential infrastructure, with increased penalties for nighttime offenses.

item.title: Lula enviará novo nome ao STF antes das eleições, diz líder do PT
item.description: PT House leader Pedro Uczai said President Lula will submit a new Supreme Court nominee before the 2026 elections, following the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias — the first such rejection in 132 years. He downplayed recent government losses, including the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetry Bill, stating the Planalto will not retaliate against legislative setbacks.

item.title: Lula quer ministro 'mágico' que arranje mais dinheiro para ampliar pacote do crédito
item.description: The Lula government is seeking a minister capable of securing additional resources to expand its credit package, after the Desenrola Brasil program fell short of expectations. The debt renegotiation initiative failed to reach its target audience despite the volume of funds involved. Pressure is mounting within the governing coalition to deliver broader access to credit.

item.title: PT faz jantar de arrecadação em Brasília para celebrar 46 anos
item.description: The PT held a fundraising dinner in Brasília to celebrate its 46th anniversary, attended by party president Edinho Silva, Minister José Guimarães, and congressional leader Pedro Uczai. The event gathered around 200 participants, with tickets averaging R$1,000, and announced a collective fundraising campaign for May 15. Edinho emphasized the strategic importance of such gatherings to strengthen the party ahead of future challenges.

item.title: Governo Lula evitará vingança contra o Congresso, diz líder do PT
item.description: PT leader Pedro Uczai said the Lula government will not seek revenge against Congress after two recent defeats: the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court and the overturning of a veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which reduces penalties for Jair Bolsonaro. Despite this, the Planoalto had considered retaliatory measures against Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The government will focus on three legislative priorities in 2026: the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule, a bill on rare earths, and reducing fuel taxes.

item.title: O novo Desenrola: até onde vai o alívio para os endividados? - O Assunto #1712
item.description: The federal government launched the new Desenrola in March 2026, allowing partial use of FGTS to pay off debts and blocking access to betting sites for participants. The program aims to reduce household debt, which reached 82.8 million Brazilians (half of all households), but economists warn that tight public finances prevent interest rate cuts, limiting relief. Analysts also note political motivation: the government seeks to regain popularity in an election year through direct-impact measures on citizens' wallets.

item.title: Ministro da Fazenda diz que governo não será “sócio da guerra”
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated the government will not bear additional fiscal costs from the Middle East war but will maintain temporary fuel tax cuts, offset by extra petroleum revenues. He noted Petrobras' pricing policy helps curb volatility, and state adherence to the measures ends May 5, 2026, with a review after roughly two months.

item.title: Derrota no Senado serve para tirar Lula da zona de conforto
item.description: Lula's nomination to the Supreme Court was sabotaged by Davi Alcolumbre, who sought to install his own ally, while the right-wing seized the moment to undermine ministers seen as having questionable reputations, aiming to strengthen their Senate influence. The episode reveals a political-institutional struggle for control of the Court, with both sides using the process to place loyal allies on the STF.

item.title: País precisa sair do labirinto
item.description: Brazil is trapped in a political labyrinth built by anti-PT and anti-Bolsonarism, which dominate discourse and exclude moderate voters. Rejection of both sides exceeds 80%, leaving only a small, insignificant faction without influence, lost in hollow coalitions. This antagonism stalls the future and hope, hostage to forces that destroy rather than build.

item.title: Lula deve usar encontro com Trump para tentar mostrar força em momento de crise com o Congresso
item.description: Lula aims to use his meeting with Donald Trump to showcase international prestige and counterbalance the domestic political crisis triggered by the historic rejection of his STF nominee, seeking to reinforce his global leadership image and counter opposition narratives of him being a 'lame duck'.

item.title: Conselho de ética da Câmara vota punição para deputados que ocuparam a Mesa Diretora
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Ethics Council will vote on Tuesday on a report recommending a two-month suspension of deputies Marcos Pollon (PL-MS), Zé Trovão (PL-SC), and Marcel Van Hattem (Novo-RS) for occupying the Directorate Board on August 6, 2025, deemed a breach of parliamentary decorum. Rapporteur Moses Rodrigues (União Brasil-CE) argues the act aimed to disrupt legislative function, while the accused deputies claim the protest was political and protected by parliamentary immunity and the right to assemble.

item.title: Por que Lula está usando chapéu em público? Conheça o modelo escolhido pelo presidente
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has resumed wearing a Panama hat in public following medical advice after the removal of a basal cell carcinoma lesion from his scalp on April 24. The hat is being used to protect the healing area, and this is not the first time Lula has worn it — he also used it after head surgeries in 2024. The chosen hat is a Panama model by Sarquis by ABA, a style historically associated with Brazilian public figures.

item.title: Fies: entenda como será a renegociação de dívidas do crédito universitário e como aderir
item.description: The government launched Desenrola Brasil 2026, which includes renegotiation of FIES student loan debts with discounts of up to 99% for CadÚnico-registered students and up to 77% for others, plus credit clearing for debts up to R$100. The program allows lump-sum or installment payments (up to 150 times), with over 1 million students expected to benefit.

item.title: Pesquisas indicam incertezas para PT e PL e vantagem de aliados de Flávio em maiores palanques
item.description: The Genial/Quaest polls from April 2026 show uncertainty for PT candidates and an advantage for allies of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in Brazil’s two largest electoral colleges, signaling a challenging scenario for the left and strengthening of the Bolsonarist base in key state races.

item.title: Rejeição a Messias sinaliza isolamento de Lula na eleição e aliança restrita à esquerda
item.description: The historic rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF was interpreted by party leaders as a sign of President Lula's political isolation in the 2026 election. This development reflects a reorganization of forces around Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), who is tied with Lula in second-round voting intention polls.

item.title: Governo Lula prioriza RJ e MG em publicidade nas redes para anúncios regionais
item.description: The Lula government prioritized regional advertising in Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, which accounted for 42% of the R$5.7 million spent on location-based boosts on Facebook and Instagram between October 2025 and April 14, 2026. The investments were managed by the federal government's communications team, focusing on regional reach via Meta platforms. This strategy underscores the electoral significance of these states for the PT in the 2026 elections.

item.title: STF marca julgamento para decidir se Bolsonaro poderia ter bloqueado cidadãos em redes oficiais
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) has scheduled May 20 to rule on two cases examining whether former President Jair Bolsonaro could block citizens on his official social media accounts while in office. The cases, reported by Minister Cármen Lúcia and Minister André Mendonça, address the boundaries of free speech and governmental account moderation powers.

item.title: Zema propõe mais tempo de contribuição para aposentadoria e atenua fala sobre trabalho infantil
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate for the Novo party, stated that if elected, he would propose a new pension reform increasing the required contribution time for retirement, not ruling out also raising the minimum age. He said the measure is necessary to ensure the system's sustainability.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro ironiza encontro entre Lula E Trump: 'E a soberania nacional?'
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro mocked the meeting between Lula and Trump in the U.S., calling the Brazilian president a 'malandro' on social media. He questioned the defense of national sovereignty during the visit, implying Lula was acting opportunistically or submissively to U.S. interests.

item.title: Lula libera crédito extraordinário de R$ 305 milhões para desastres ambientais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a provisional measure allocating R$ 305 million in extraordinary credit for emergency relief efforts targeting victims of environmental disasters across Brazil. The funds will support immediate assistance such as shelter, food, healthcare, and basic reconstruction in areas impacted by floods, landslides, and other extreme weather events.

item.title: Zema pendura 'melancia digital' no pescoço ao repetir o pior de Bolsonaro
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for presidency under the Novo party, is adopting speeches and phrases from Jair Bolsonaro to attract Bolsonarist voters, repeating the ex-president’s strategy of provocation to gain media and social media attention. This approach aims to inflame debates and capture public attention by imitating Bolsonaro’s polarizing communication style.

item.title: Durigan diz esperar cortes de juros como complemento ao Desenrola e nega que política fiscal atrapalhe BC
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the government expects the ongoing Selic rate cuts to complement the effects of the new Desenrola Brasil debt renegotiation program. He denied that fiscal policy hinders the Central Bank’s current interest rate reduction cycle and emphasized measures such as a one-year betting ban for program participants to prevent re-indebtedness.

item.title: Alckmin lamenta rejeição de Messias ao STF e diz que Lula está definindo uma nova indicação
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin lamented the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF, praising his qualifications and public service, and stated that President Lula is defining a new nomination. He noted the vacancy harms the Court's functioning, already burdened with cases, and said the government is engaging in dialogue with Congress to move forward.

item.title: “Sou igual à maioria dos brasileiros”, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate for Novo, defended his candidacy in a UOL interview, emphasizing that his private-sector background distinguishes him from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. He stated he is 'like most Brazilians' because he had to work to build his wealth, contrasting himself with politicians from hereditary or privileged backgrounds.

item.title: Associação pede ao STF que rejeição de Jorge Messias à Corte pelo Senado seja anulada
item.description: The Civitas Association for Citizenship and Culture filed an ADPF with the STF seeking to annul the Senate session that rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Court, arguing that Senate President Davi Alcolumbre prematurely declared 'he will lose by eight,' violating voting secrecy and constituting a procedural flaw. The group requests a new open vote, but constitutional consultants told JOTA that the STF is likely to dismiss the case on procedural grounds due to lack of standing, without ruling on the merits.

item.title: Lula assina MP que libera crédito extraordinário de R$ 305 milhões para regiões atingidas por desastres
item.description: President Lula signed a Provisional Measure releasing R$ 305 million in extraordinary credit for civil protection and defense actions in regions affected by climate disasters, particularly in the Northeast, where heavy rains have caused at least eight deaths since May 1. The funds will support emergency relief, humanitarian assistance, and restoration of essential services, sourced from the Union's excess revenue.

item.title: Zema comete gafe em entrevista e diz que no Brasil “falta ladrão”
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (NOVO) made a gaffe during an interview by stating that 'Brazil lacks thieves', intending to criticize corruption but using an unfortunate phrasing. He corrected himself after interviewer intervention and reiterated that his future vice-presidential running mate must have a 'clean record', which he said is hard to find. Zema also discussed public security, advocating for a dedicated public safety department in the Justice Ministry led by police officers and supporting body cameras only during special operations.

item.title: Novo pede apuração de viagem do diretor da PF paga pelo Master
item.description: The Novo party filed two representations against Federal Police Director-General Andrei Rodrigues, alleging administrative impropriety and conflict of interest, after his trip to London for the 1st Legal Forum — Brazil of Ideas was fully funded by Banco Master, an institution under investigation by the PF. The April 2024 event cost approximately R$ 3.2 million and included sponsorship from British American Tobacco and FS Security, along with private whisky tastings at a Mayfair club. The representations, signed by DF Senate pre-candidate Sebastião Coelho, were submitted to the Federal Prosecutor’s Office in DF and the Presidency’s Public Ethics Commission.

item.title: Entidade pede a inelegibilidade de Flávio Bolsonaro após culto com Malafaia
item.description: The Secular Brazil Movement filed a complaint against pastor Silas Malafaia and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for alleged early electioneering during a religious service at the Vitória em Cristo Assembly of God, claiming the event was politically motivated rather than religious. The group demands up to eight years of ineligibility and a R$ 25,000 fine for all attending politicians, plus a Federal Revenue investigation into potential misuse of the church’s resources.

item.title: Gleisi critica Alcolumbre e diz que governo não pode entrar nas eleições com 'inimigo dentro de casa'
item.description: Federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) criticized Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) for voting against Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF and for overturning Lula's vetoes on the Dosimetria bill, which benefits Bolsonaro. She accused Alcolumbre of acting as a party leader and aligning with pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, stating the government cannot enter elections with an 'enemy within the house'.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro ironiza encontro entre Lula e Trump: ‘E a soberania nacional?’
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro mocked President Lula's meeting with Donald Trump in Washington, accusing the PT leader of hypocrisy for defending national sovereignty while allegedly negotiating with the U.S. in favor of elites. He recalled that Lula had previously accused Flávio Bolsonaro of being submissive to American interests, particularly regarding rare earth exploration, and highlighted the contrast between Lula's rhetoric for his base and his actions toward the U.S.

item.title: Governo não pode disputar eleições com ‘inimigo dentro de casa’, diz Gleisi
item.description: Institutional Relations Minister Gleisi Hoffmann criticized the government's recent setbacks in Congress, attributing them to an articulation led by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and supported by center-right leaders. She warned that the government cannot enter an electoral dispute with an 'enemy within,' stating that only those who will stand with the government in elections should be considered allies. The setbacks include the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' Supreme Court nomination and Congress overturning Lula's veto on a bill reducing sentences for those involved in the 2022 coup attempt.

item.title: El Supremo de Venezuela se reorganiza con suplentes mientras se buscan nuevos candidatos
item.description: Ten magistrates of Venezuela's Supreme Tribunal of Justice's Plenary Chamber have formally retired or resigned, with their positions being filled by alternates. The National Assembly, controlled by Chavismo, has already begun the legislative process to appoint new justices to the country's highest court. The move follows weeks of speculation about the restructuring of the judiciary.

item.title: Moraes rejeita revisar pena de Débora do Batom, condenada pelo 8/1
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes rejected a request by Débora do Batom's defense to immediately reduce her sentence under the Dosimetria Bill, stating the bill has not yet been promulgated. Débora, sentenced to 14 years for participating in the January 8, 2023, coup attempts and graffitiing 'Perdeu, mané' on the statue of Justice with lipstick, is currently serving house arrest in Paulínia, SP, under electronic monitoring. Moraes emphasized that although Congress overturned the presidential veto on April 30, 2026, the law is not in force until officially promulgated.
